errors.problem: The letter i is the imaginary unit and also the axis index bound by the inner sum in the same exponent (the page set i as the axis index just before). The formula is otherwise right for the paper's normalization (F_q u)_k=(1/q)\sum_j u_j e^{-2\pi i jk/q} (lines 3506-3510), tensored over axes.

errors.quote: This bound needs power-of-two lengths, so it does not apply directly to the prime lengths $s_i$ of the integer product; the identity below supplies power-of-two transforms instead.
errors.problem: An O(q log q) operation count does not need power-of-two lengths. Prime lengths reach it too, for example by Bluestein chirps, which the argument itself uses. Only the radix-2 butterfly needs a power of two. The paper's reason for resampling is different: 'The transform lengths needed for the integer product are pairwise coprime, whereas the synthetic transforms use powers of two. Gaussian resampling connects these two shapes' (lines 3499-3501).

errors.quote: Fixed-point algorithms approximate each with error less than $p^2$
errors.problem: The page never gives the unit of error. In the paper, an approximation has error E when 2^p||\tilde L u - Lu|| < E (lines 3529-3531), so the absolute error is less than p^2 2^{-p}. Read as an absolute bound, 'less than p^2' (and 'less than dp^2' later) says nothing about values of norm at most 1.
